Nothing to set up. Phone-OTP login (auth.identifier: phone) and hook/flow SMS steps deliver via the shared platform number.
Daily quota: 5/day free (enough to develop OTP), 200/day paid. `benmore sms <app>` / dashboard → Email & SMS show usage.

The daily quota is counted per owner account as well as per app. Each text counts against the app and against the account that owns it; the account's allowance is the per-app quota times its live-app allowance: the live apps the owner's plan includes plus the extra live-app slots it bought (5 apps' worth on Pro, 25 on Scale, and one app's worth on free, which includes no live app). An operator-raised per-account app limit counts as before, and an account with more published apps than that keeps each published app's quota. Apps still in development add nothing: an account using each of its published apps up to the per-app quota is never refused by the account allowance, and one sending at full per-app quota from more apps in development than it has live slots is. What an app sent stays on its owner's day after the app is deleted; deleting an app and creating another does not start a new quota (the text is refused with `the account's daily SMS allowance is used up`). SMS status reports `account_quota_used_today` and `account_quota_daily_limit`.

Destinations restricted to allowed calling prefixes (default +1 US/Canada) - international toll fraud (AIT) protection. Need another country? support@benmore.tech. `+1` means US states and Canada only; the other countries and territories that dial as +1 (Jamaica, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, Guam, ...) and the 900/976 premium codes are refused unless the operator lists their own prefix.

Per-recipient velocity cap (5 msgs / 10 min) on top of the quota. The cap counts messages the provider accepted, per sending app - a refused request (no quota, paused, throttled, provider error) does not use a slot, and one app's messages do not use another app's budget for the same number.

The per-recipient cap also has a bucket per owner account and number, sized 5 per 10 minutes for each app's worth of the account's allowance (its live-app allowance, as for the daily quota, so each app within it can still send its own 5). An app created after another was deleted starts with an empty bucket of its own but not a new one for the account, so it cannot text the same number again past the cap; the refusal reads `SMS rate limit exceeded ... across the account's apps`.
